title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades & Customer Requirements
author: Ayesha Rao
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference guidance for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on‑prem packaged installations). It covers: reference architectures, on‑prem packaging & installation patterns, day‑2 operational runbooks (monitoring, backups, capacity), and detailed upgrade + rollback procedures. A separate customer requirements checklist is included to streamline presales and delivery.

Audience
- Solutions engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and customer IT/security teams responsible for private deployments.

Goals
- Provide repeatable, audited steps for safe install, day‑2 operations, and upgrades.
- Specify minimum customer network, security, and capacity requirements.
- Reduce upgrade downtime risk via staged rollouts and automated validation checks.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments: VPC-hosted (customer VPC with Private Control Plane) and on‑prem (air‑gapped or connected).
- Assumes customer provides compute (GPU nodes or compatible CPUs for quantized models), KMS integration, and network ACLs as specified in the Customer Requirements table.
- For Dedicated-managed hardware (Redwood-provisioned) follow the Dedicated docs; this doc focuses on customer‑owned infra.

Owners & escalation
- Service owner: eng-private-deployments (primary SE: Ayesha Rao).
- Escalation path: SE -> Deployment Team -> Infra SRE -> Oncall (pager: eng-oncall).

Reference architectures (high level)

1) VPC deployment (recommended for cloud customers)
- Topology: Customer VPC with private subnets for compute, a public subnet for a bastion and optional NAT gateway. Control plane endpoints in customer VPC peered to Redwood control plane or connected via PrivateLink/VPN.
- Components:
  - Inference cluster (GPU node pool) behind a private load balancer
  - Data plane agents (metrics, logging forwarder) in private subnets
  - KMS endpoint (customer-managed HSM or cloud KMS) for key operations
  - Artifact storage (S3-compatible, with bucket policies) for model artifacts and images
- Sizing guidance: start with min 4x A10/A100-equivalent GPUs for small production; scale to pools per model profile. See Capacity Sizing table below.

2) On‑prem air‑gapped deployment
- Topology: customer datacenter with isolated network segments for inference, management and storage. Appliances or VM hosts for GPU compute.
- Packaging: OCI images + downloadable model artifact tarballs; installation via our on‑prem installer (rpm/deb) or Helm charts for k8s-connected environments.
- Required services: local artifact registry (Harbor), local NTP, syslog/ELK or Splunk forwarder, KMS/HSM (optional).

3) Hybrid (edge + central control)
- Small inference clusters at edge sites for low latency; central model registry and policy control in customer core. Automated model sync and health checks.

Configuration & packaging options
- Kubernetes (preferred): helm/redwood-operator + CRDs for model deployments. Supports autoscaling, rolling upgrade hooks, and integration with cluster autoscaler.
- Bare metal: systemd units + containerd runtime, managed by our installer. GPU drivers (NVIDIA driver + CUDA) must be preinstalled.
- VM-based: provided images for common hypervisors; use the included system agent for orchestration.

Packaging artifacts delivered to customers
- redwood-installer-{version}.tar.gz (installer binary, manifests, schema)
- helm/redwood-operator-{version}.tgz
- models/{model-name}-{version}.tar.gz (signed, checksummed)
- packaging/README.md (installation checklist and offline install steps)

Customer requirements library (checklist)
- Purpose: single-source checklist for pre-sales and deployment engineering. Provide this to customers during scoping.

Minimal network & security requirements (tableized):
| Requirement | Minimum | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| VPC subnets | 2 private subnets (multi-AZ) + optional public subnet | Private subnets for compute; route tables must allow egress to artifact storage or proxy. |
| NAT / egress | NAT Gateway or proxy | Required for image pulls unless fully air-gapped. |
| KMS | Cloud KMS or HSM available | For encryption of keys; Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, and PKCS11 HSM integrations. |
| Artifact storage | S3-compatible, TLS | Bucket policy with object versioning recommended. |
| Ports | 443 outbound for control plane; 8443 (optional) for local admin | See full port list in packaging/README. |
| Service account | Kubernetes service account with RBAC | Minimal privileges: create/patch pods, list secrets, create jobs (detailed policy in RBAC snippet). |

Compute & capacity (sizing table)
| Workload profile | Typical nodes | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Low throughput (dev) | 1-2 x A10 or equivalent | Single replica per model. |
| Production (multi-tenant) | 4-8 x A100 or equivalent | Use dedicated pools per model family; enable batcher. |
| High throughput (LLM serving) | 16+ GPUs with sharding | Use model parallel or pipeline parallel as recommended in model onboarding doc. |

Onboarding & install checklist (short)
1. Confirm network, IAM, and KMS requirements with customer.
2. Validate GPU drivers / hardware compatibility (NVIDIA driver >= 525 / CUDA >= 11.8 for recommended builds).
3. Provide customer with redwood-installer and signed model artifacts.
4. Run preflight checks (installer --preflight).
5. Run installation in staging; validate inference, metrics, and logs.
6. Promote to production following the rollout policy below.

Preflight command examples
- Installer preflight (connected): ./redwood-installer --preflight --config ./customer-config.yaml
- Helm dry-run: helm install redwood ./redwood-operator-1.6.0.tgz --namespace redwood --dry-run
- GPU check: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv

Day‑2 operations runbook (SRE-focused)

Monitoring & alerting
- Metrics: token latency p50/p95/p99, requests per second, GPU utilization, batch queue length, KV cache hit rate.
- Logs: Application logs to local aggregator; forward to customer SIEM or Redwood support channel for escalations.
- Default SLOs: 99.9% successful inference responses per 30d window; p95 latency < 250ms for small models, < 1s for LLMs (configurable per-customer SLA).

Standard alerts (examples)
- High error rate: error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes -> Pager (oncall)
- Latency breach: p95 latency > SLA threshold for 10 minutes -> Pager (oncall)
- GPU OOMs: any OOMs detected -> Alert to Deployment Team and SE channel
- Disk pressure: /var/lib/ephemeral > 85% -> Ticket to Infra team

Runbook: pod crash/restart loop
1. Check pod events: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood
2. Inspect logs: kubectl logs <pod> -c runtime -n redwood --previous
3. If OOMKilled or driver errors, collect dmesg and nvidia-smi output and escalate to infra-sre.
4. Replace pod with: kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood
5. If persistent, follow rollback procedure for last deploy.

Backups and artifact management
- Model artifacts: immutable, versioned in artifact registry. On upgrade, previous model tarballs are retained for 30 days (configurable).
- Config backups: etcd snapshots (for k8s): schedule daily snapshots and store in encrypted object storage.
- Key backups: follow customer's KMS/HSM backup procedure — Redwood does not store plaintext keys.

Capacity planning & autoscaling guidance
- Use cluster-autoscaler with GPU-aware scheduling and preemptible instance pools for cost optimization.
- Maintain 10–20% spare GPU headroom for model warmups and burst traffic.

Upgrade & rollback procedures (safe upgrade pattern)

Principles
- Always stage upgrades in a staging environment that mirrors prod (node types, sequence lengths).
- Preserve previous artifact versions locally for immediate rollback.
- Automate canary validation including functional tests, latency checks, and model quality checks (sample prompt eval).

High-level upgrade steps
1. Prepare artifacts: upload new operator image, runtime image, and model artifacts to artifact store and tag with release-{date}.
2. Run canary in staging: deploy to staging cluster; run smoke tests and perf benchmarks.
3. Canary in prod: deploy to 10% of nodes (label selector) with traffic split via routing policy. Monitor 30–60 minutes.
4. Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with health checks at each stage.
5. Post‑upgrade validation: run automated sample prompts, check metrics and logs for anomalies for 24–72 hours.

Automated health checks (example list)
- API health endpoints return 200 within 100ms.
- Inference p95 latency not degraded > 10% from baseline.
- Model output quality: regression tests against baseline prompt set show no more than 1% drop in classification accuracy or expected metric.

Rollback procedure (immediate rollback)
1. Trigger: sustained error_rate > 0.5% or latency > threshold after canary or rollout stage.
2. Steps:
  a. Pause rollout: kubectl rollout pause deployment/redwood-operator -n redwood
  b. Repoint routing to previous model image/tag for affected routes (route policy or traffic-split).
  c. Roll back operator/runtime: kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood --to-revision=<previous>
  d. Validate: run smoke tests and check health endpoints.
3. Postmortem: open incident, collect logs, and run regression triage per regression-triage playbook.

Manual rollback (if automation fails)
- Restore etcd snapshot from before the deployment (documented snapshot timestamp).
- Redeploy previous helm charts and model artifacts from the artifact bucket.

Upgrade windows and change management
- Preferred upgrade windows: off-peak in customer timezone, min 2 hours for canaries and validations.
- Change approvals: SE + customer ops approval required for production upgrades. For air‑gapped customers, SE to confirm artifact delivery and checksum matches before upgrade.

Safety checklist for upgrades
- Previous images and artifacts retained and accessible.
- Preflight tests passed in staging.
- Rollback playbook available to oncall.
- Customer notified with escalation contacts.

Operational runbook snippets (commands)
- Rollout status: kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood
- Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood --to-revision=2
- Snapshot etcd (k8s): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /backups/etcd-$(date +%F).db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.pem --cert=/etc/etcd/cert.pem --key=/etc/etcd/key.pem

Packaging & release frequency
- Minor patch releases: monthly for critical fixes and dependency updates.
- Major releases: quarterly with release notes and migration notes.
- Security patches: out‑of‑band with CVE advisory and targeted upgrade instructions.

Compliance & audit notes
- Audit logging: all control-plane and admin actions are logged and forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Data residency: model artifacts and telemetry may be stored in customer-owned storage when requested.
- Penetration tests: recommend customer complete pentest pre-prod and annually for on‑prem deployments.

Appendix A — Example RBAC snippet (k8s)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: redwood-runtime-role
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods", "pods/log", "secrets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "patch"]

Appendix B — Troubleshooting table (common issues)
| Symptom | Likely cause | First actions |
|---|---|---|
| High inference latency | Cold cache, no batching, overloaded GPU | Warm cache, increase batch size, scale out GPU pool |
| Model fails to load | Missing artifact, checksum mismatch | Verify artifact in registry, compare sha256, redeploy artifact |
| TLS handshake failures | Expired certs or incorrect chain | Verify cert expiry, restart ingress, check SNI settings |
